title: DOJ Office of Legal Counsel Opinion Rejects ADA/Rehabilitation Act Integration Mandate for State Institutionalization
description_short: DOJ Office of Legal Counsel Opinion Rejects ADA/Rehabilitation Act Integration Mandate for State Institutionalization
description_medium: On June 18, 2026, the Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion concluding that neither Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act nor Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act imposed an integration mandate on states in their treatment of individuals with mental disabilities, nor authorized executive agencies to impose such a mandate. The opinion stated the Supreme Court in Olmstead v. L.C.
description_long: On June 18, 2026, the Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion concluding that neither Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act nor Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act imposed an integration mandate on states in their treatment of individuals with mental disabilities, nor authorized executive agencies to impose such a mandate. The opinion stated the Supreme Court in Olmstead v. L.C. did not hold that those statutes require states to treat mentally disabled patients in the most integrated setting. The opinion acknowledged its interpretation is out of step with the common understanding of Olmstead within the federal courts. Senator Tammy Duckworth, with Schumer and Durbin, led Senate Democrats in introducing a resolution calling on DOJ to rescind the opinion. Correction/source notes clarify: The official DOJ OLC opinion is dated June 18, 2026, not June 22, 2026 as the card states. The DOJ's own opinion page and the Duckworth resolution both cite June 18, 2026 as the issuance date. On January 25, 2025, Trump told reporters he wanted to just clean out Gaza and have Egypt and Jordan permanently absorb its more than 2 million Palestinian residents, calling Gaza a mess and offering Palestinians a beautiful new land.
description_long: On January 25, 2025, Trump told reporters he wanted to just clean out Gaza and have Egypt and Jordan permanently absorb its more than 2 million Palestinian residents, calling Gaza a mess and offering Palestinians a beautiful new land. On February 4, 2025, standing beside Netanyahu, Trump said Palestinians had no alternative but to leave and that the US would take over the territory to rebuild it as a Riviera of the Middle East. Human Rights Watch called it an alarming escalation of forced displacement and ethnic cleansing. Both Egypt and Jordan flatly refused. Germany, Australia, Ireland, the UK, Brazil, China, and Russia all rejected the plan. Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich welcomed the proposal and said he was preparing an operational plan to implement it. Linked source: “Trump suggests permanently displacing Palestinians from Gaza.” This account separates the documented event from broader conclusions and does not infer unstated motives, legal results, or downstream effects.
